t: The principal Crusader state, founded after the First Crusade took Jerusalem in July 1099.
A small Frankish elite ruled a mostly Muslim and Eastern Christian population, relying on castles, military orders and Italian fleets.
Saladin’s victory at Hattin in 1187 broke it; the kingdom survived on the coast until the Mamluks took Acre in 1291.
dyk: The kingdom minted gold coins imitating Fatimid dinars, with Arabic inscriptions; after papal objections in the 1250s they carried Christian texts in Arabic.
ev: Baldwin I is crowned the first king at Bethlehem
Tyre falls to the Franks and a Venetian fleet
Baldwin IV defeats Saladin at Montgisard
Saladin destroys the Frankish army at Hattin and takes Jerusalem
Frederick II regains Jerusalem by treaty
The Mamluks take Acre, ending the kingdom

f.founder: Godfrey of Bouillon; Baldwin I (first king)
f.successor: Mamluk Sultanate; title passed to the Kingdom of Cyprus
